I have resolved the issue where sending email messages on system hostnames or domains containing non-ASCII characters failed when the message encoding was non-unicode (e.g. `iso-8859-1`).

### Cause
When generating the `Message-ID` email header using standard library `make_msgid`, non-ASCII domain names from `socket.getfqdn()` or `DNS_NAME` were embedded directly into the header string as unicode. When header encoding (such as `iso-8859-1`) was subsequently applied to the `Message-ID` header, Python failed with a `UnicodeEncodeError` or encoded the header with invalid RFC 2047 format.

### Solution
1. Updated `django.core.mail.utils.CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()` to convert non-ASCII domain names to IDNA ASCII punycode using `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`.
2. Updated `django.core.mail.message.EmailMessage.message()` to ensure domain names passed to `make_msgid()` are converted to IDNA ASCII punycode.
3. Added a regression test `test_unicode_dns` in [`tests/mail/tests.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-m1uffkor/tests/mail/tests.py#L407-L412).
